subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers salvage the existing conflicting fork PR or close it and authorize a narrow replacement fix for this issue?
rationale: The issue is valid, but an open non-maintainer fork PR with closing syntax already owns the exact bug and cannot be updated by maintainers, so automation should not race it without a branch-path choice.

options.title: Authorize a narrow replacement
options.body: Open a maintainer-editable replacement that covers current sync and async session-list paths, then close or supersede the conflicting fork PR.

options.title: Ask the fork author to rebase
options.body: Keep this issue paired to the existing fork PR and wait for the author to resolve conflicts and add current real-behavior proof.

options.title: Adopt the fork manually
options.body: A maintainer can cherry-pick the useful diff into an OpenClaw branch because the fork PR does not allow maintainer edits.

recommendation.title: Authorize a narrow replacement
recommendation.body: Open a maintainer-editable replacement that covers current sync and async session-list paths, then close or supersede the conflicting fork PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Among the history owners, this login has merger and adjacent session-display ownership signals and is the best available branch-path decision owner.
